verdict.rationale: pnpm's docs describe built-in workspaces that unite multiple projects in one repository, a single shared lockfile, and the workspace: protocol, which resolves only to local packages and still allows publishing. Community users migrating 20+ package monorepos from Lerna corroborate that the built-in monorepo support works well. Occasional symlink glitches with multiple package versions were reported, but these do not contradict the core capability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage many packages in one monorepo with workspaces sharing a single lockfile and cross-linked local dependencies

citations.quote: First-class monorepos: the workspace protocol for local packages, filtering to run tasks on just the projects you touched, and a single lockfile for everything.
You can create a workspace to unite multiple projects inside a single repository.
When this protocol is used, pnpm will refuse to resolve to anything other than a local workspace package.
Several projects can share one lockfile.
everything on pnpm's built-in monorepo support just works, nice & easy & fast.
